topics.name: Biodiversity loss

rows.t: wildlife down 73% since 1970 (Living Planet Report) · India: 3,682 tigers (>70% of world), 22,446 elephants, but protected areas only 5.71% of land
laws diluted: jail → fines for minor offences <button class="hs chipx" data-h="2">Jan Vishwas Act 2023</button>
weak monitoring + many BMCs exist only on paper
invasive species (Lantana) + climate change (coral bleaching)
poaching and wildlife trade (rhinos, pangolins worst hit, 2024; 100+ birds and turtles seized in Jalaun) + communities left out
habitat lost to infrastructure and mining (≈77% of world's mines within 50 km of Key Biodiversity Areas)
finance gap (≈$700 billion a year worldwide; India's NBSAP needs ₹81,664 crore a year)
Centre–state fights (Kerala wants power to declare "vermin")
Environment: lost pollination, clean water, carbon storage · Economy: forests support ≈275 million livelihoods · Health: zoonoses (Nipah)

hs.b:
• Latitude 8°–37°N (tropical Kerala → temperate J&K) + rainfall 100 mm → 11,000 mm (Cherrapunji); wet Western Ghats vs dry Deccan only ≈100 km apart
  • Long coast, big rivers + cut-off islands → endemism (Andamans, Lakshadweep) + old Gondwana block → long time to evolve
  • Northeast = meeting point of 3 realms (Indian, Indo-Malayan, Indo-Chinese)
  • Hotspot criteria: at least 1,500 endemic vascular plants + lost at least 70% of original habitat

• The most individuals (or resource use) an area can support for ever without degrading its resources
  • Exceeded → aquifers, rivers, grass run down + sudden population crash + overshoot lowers future capacity (an overfished lake never gets its fish back)
  • In planning: carrying-capacity studies for hill towns (SC asked Himalayan states, 2023) + caps on tourists and vehicles + basis for EIA and master plans
  • Failed: Joshimath sinking 2023 = capacity ignored

• Amends 42 central laws (incl. EPA 1986, Air Act 1981): jail → penalties for minor offences, decided by adjudicating officers
  • Fines go into an Environment Protection Fund (EPA Section 15: ₹10,000 to ₹15 lakh)
  • Criticism: SC calls it "toothless" + harm continues (Futala Lake, illegal quarrying in Kerala forests) → fix: fines that deter + keep jail for serious harm

• Transshipment port (Galathea Bay) + airport + 450 MW power plant + township, near the Malacca, Sunda, Lombok straits → cargo + defence
  • Concerns: Shompen (PVTG) and Nicobarese displaced + leatherback turtle nesting + ≈9.6 lakh trees cut + mangroves lost + sits on the 2004 tsunami megathrust
  • Forest rights not settled under FRA (A&N says its 1956 Aboriginal Tribes law, under which the administration alone can divert land, is enough; FRA needs Gram Sabha consent) · NGT 2023 upheld clearances → committee cleared the port again (Feb 2026)
  • Way forward: phased, ecologically sensitive, community-inclusive

• 1,630 people killed by animals (ADSI 2024) + Kerala declared it a state-specific disaster + elephant conflict rising (Jharkhand, West Bengal) + crop loss, retaliatory killing
  • Why: more animals, same 5% protected-area network → they spill into farms and towns (langurs misused in Gurugram)
  • Fix: National HWC Mitigation Strategy 2021–26 + SOPs (tiger, leopard, elephant) + early warnings (SMS, sensors, GPS collars) + bee-hive and solar fences + crops elephants avoid (chilli, citrus, ginger)
  • SC: ₹10 lakh for each human death + landscape approach + corridors

• 2022 amendment: 6 schedules → 4 (I highest protection, II high, III plants, IV CITES species)
  • Protected areas: National Parks (no human use) → Sanctuaries (some rights) → Conservation Reserves (buffers, corridors) → Community Reserves (local land)
  • Bodies: NBWL (PM chairs) + NTCA (tigers) + WCCB (wildlife crime) + CZA (zoos)
  • Base: Art 48A (DPSP) + Art 51A(g) + forests and wild animals on the Concurrent List (42nd Amendment, 1976)
  • Worked: Kaziranga (zero rhino poaching 2022) + TX2 met in 2018 · Failed: Great Indian Bustard (Schedule I since 1972, ≈130 left)

• Regulates access to biological resources, stops biopiracy, shares benefits · 3 tiers: NBA → State Biodiversity Boards → BMCs (1.4 lakh, keep People's Biodiversity Registers)
  • Biodiversity Heritage Sites (Kaya Kalp Vriksh, Punjab; Arittapatti, Madurai → tungsten mine cancelled 2025)
  • 2023 amendment + 2025 rules: jail → fines + AYUSH exempt + digital sequence data covered + benefit share 0.2–0.6% (5%+ high value), 60–75% to local communities
  • Worked: Kani tribe, Kerala (Jeevani drug, royalty shared) · Failed: Bt brinjal biopiracy case (2011, dragged for years)
  • Traditional knowledge: TKDL + PPVFR Act 2001 + GI Act 1999 → problems: biopiracy, poor records → pay TK holders + benefit sharing under Nagoya

• Buffers around protected areas under EPA 1986: prohibited (mining, polluting industry) / regulated (tree felling, hotels) / permitted (local farming)
  • Worked: Mahabaleshwar–Panchgani (2001) · Mixed: SC's 1-km ESZ round every PA (2022) relaxed in 2023 · Failed: Netala bypass, Bhagirathi ESZ (2025)

• Chipko (1973, Uttarakhand): non-violent hugging of trees → commercial logging banned in the Himalaya
  • Appiko (1983, Karnataka) + Silent Valley (1984: dam dropped → National Park) + Anti-Tehri Dam + Narmada Bachao Andolan (1985–)
  • NGOs and rehabilitation PYQs (2024, 2016) → see EIA

• KMGBF (CBD COP15, 2022): 23 targets by 2030: protect 30% of land and sea (30x30) + restore 30% + halve invasive species + cut $500 billion harmful subsidies + raise $200 billion a year
  • Replaced the Aichi targets (none of 20 fully met by 2020) · Protected Planet 2024: 17.6% land, 8.4% ocean protected
  • COP16, Cali (2024): Cali Fund (companies using digital sequence data pay 1% of profits or 0.1% of revenue, voluntary) + permanent body for Indigenous peoples · ran out of quorum, resumed in Rome 2025
  • Gaps: Cali Fund voluntary (first private payment only Nov 2025) + ≈700 billion dollars a year finance gap → fix: binding DSI payments + Kunming Biodiversity Fund

• NBSAP 2024–30: 23 national targets matched to KMGBF + whole-of-government (23 ministries) + whole-of-society · released at Cali, one of 44 countries on time
  • Runs through NBA → SBB → BMC + BIOFIN (₹81,664 crore a year needed)
  • 7th national report to the CBD: forest + tree cover 25.1% + 24.1 million ha restored (Bonn pledge 26) + 100 Ramsar sites + first counts of snow leopards (718) and river dolphins (6,327)

• CITES (1973): controls trade in endangered species (India got star tortoise, otter into Appendix I, 2019)
  • CMS (1979): migratory species (India hosted COP13, Gandhinagar 2020; GIB added) + MAB (1971): 18 biosphere reserves
  • ITPGRFA (2001): shares 64 crops (≈80% of plant diet) · India guards sovereign rights + digital sequence data = digital biopiracy risk
  • Gaps: weak enforcement (illegal wildlife trade) + targets not binding (Aichi missed) → fix: WPA Schedule IV mirrors CITES + finance for the South

• BBNJ: share benefits from high-seas genetic finds + high-seas marine protected areas + EIA for high-seas projects + help for developing countries
  • In force Jan 2026 after 60 ratifications; first COP Jan 2027 · India signed (Sep 2024), needs a domestic law to ratify
  • Issues: not universal + no punishing body + weak technology transfer → fix: ratify + build deep-sea research capacity

cm.0: Living Planet Report = WWF's report tracking how fast wild animal populations are shrinking worldwide.
cm.1: Adjudicating officer = a government officer (not a court) who decides the fine for a violation, so cases end faster.
cm.2: Environment Protection Fund = a pot where all the environmental fines go, to be spent on environmental work.
cm.3: BMC = Biodiversity Management Committee: a village- or town-level body under the BD Act that records local biodiversity and decides on its use.
cm.4: Lantana = a fast-spreading invasive shrub from South America that chokes native plants; it covers about half of India's forests and scrubland.
cm.5: Key Biodiversity Areas = sites mapped globally as the most important places for species survival.
cm.6: PVTG = Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group: the most isolated, smallest tribes, like the Shompen.
cm.7: Megathrust = the giant fault where one tectonic plate dives under another; it causes the biggest earthquakes and tsunamis.
cm.8: Vermin = an animal the Centre declares a pest (WPA Section 62) so it can be legally killed for a period, e.g. wild boar raiding crops.
cm.9: Zoonoses = diseases that jump from animals to humans (Nipah, COVID-19, rabies).
cm.10: ADSI = Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India, NCRB's yearly report.
cm.11: SOP = standard operating procedure: a fixed step-by-step drill for officials when, say, a tiger enters a village.
cm.12: Landscape approach = plan for the whole area animals move through (forests, farms, villages), not just the fenced park.
cm.13: NBWL = National Board for Wildlife (chaired by PM): clears projects inside protected areas. NTCA = National Tiger Conservation Authority (runs tiger reserves). WCCB = Wildlife Crime Control Bureau. CZA = Central Zoo Authority.
cm.14: TX2 = the global goal (2010) to double wild tigers by 2022; India did it in 2018, four years early.
cm.15: Biopiracy = companies patenting or profiting from a country's plants or traditional knowledge without permission or sharing benefits (e.g. the neem and turmeric patent fights).
cm.16: Biodiversity Heritage Site = a small, rich area a state notifies under the BD Act for protection with local people (e.g. Arittapatti, Madurai).
cm.17: AYUSH = Ayurveda, Yoga, Unani, Siddha, Homoeopathy. The 2023 amendment freed these practitioners from asking NBA before using plants.
cm.18: Digital sequence data (DSI) = genetic code of plants or animals stored online; companies can use it without touching the physical plant, so it's a new route for biopiracy.
cm.19: TKDL = Traditional Knowledge Digital Library: India's database of traditional remedies in patent-office languages, so foreigners can't patent them as new. PPVFR Act = protects new seed varieties and farmers' right to save and share seeds. GI Act = protects products tied to a place (Darjeeling tea).
cm.20: PPVFR Act 2001 (Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights): registers new plant varieties for breeders + farmers keep the right to save, use, share and sell seed (not branded). GI Act 1999: Geographical Indication tag for products tied to a place (Darjeeling tea, Basmati).
cm.21: Nagoya Protocol (2010) = CBD agreement that whoever uses another country's genetic resources must get permission and share the benefits (access and benefit sharing, ABS).
cm.22: Eco-sensitive zone = a buffer belt around a national park or sanctuary where harmful activities are banned or controlled.
cm.23: WII = Wildlife Institute of India (Dehradun); its DNA lab identifies seized animal parts to prosecute poachers.
cm.24: Eco-bridge = an overpass or underpass built for animals to cross highways and railways safely.
cm.25: NWAP = National Wildlife Action Plan (2017–31): India's wildlife roadmap (landscape approach, climate, people-centric), but not legally binding.
cm.26: BIOFIN = Biodiversity Finance Initiative (UNDP): helps countries work out how much conservation costs and where the money can come from. Cali Fund = companies that profit from digital genetic data pay into it; money goes to Indigenous and local communities.
cm.27: BRSR = Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: SEBI makes the top 1,000 listed companies disclose ESG data (energy, emissions, water, waste).
cm.28: 30x30 = protect 30% of land and 30% of oceans by 2030.
cm.29: Aichi targets = 20 biodiversity goals set in 2010 for 2020; none was fully met.
cm.30: Protected Planet Report = UN report on how much of Earth's land and sea is protected.
cm.31: DSI = digital sequence information (genetic data stored online, used by pharma and biotech). Kunming Biodiversity Fund = China-backed fund launched at COP16 to help developing countries meet KMGBF targets.
cm.32: NBSAP = National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan: each country's plan for meeting the CBD targets.
cm.33: National report = the progress report every CBD member must submit (Article 26); India's 7th says all 23 targets are on track.
cm.34: CITES = Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species: Appendix I species can't be traded commercially at all.
cm.35: CMS = Convention on Migratory Species (Bonn): protects animals that cross borders (birds, elephants, turtles).
cm.36: MAB = UNESCO's Man and Biosphere programme: biosphere reserves where conservation and local livelihoods coexist (core, buffer, transition zones).
cm.37: ITPGRFA = International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture: countries share seeds of key crops for research and breeding.
cm.38: BBNJ = Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction: the treaty for the high seas, the ocean beyond any country's 200-nautical-mile zone (about two-thirds of the ocean).

rows.t: forest 21% of area + forest and tree cover 25.17% (ISFR 2023) + 9th in forest area, 3rd in net gain (FAO 2025) + supports ≈275 million livelihoods
laws diluted (2023 amendment narrowed "forest" → ≈28% of actual forest, unrecorded, loses cover)
warming → more forest fires (36% of forest cover fire-prone)
encroachment (10,000+ acres of Odisha's reserved forests) + field-burning fires + Gram Sabhas bypassed in diversions (MP, Odisha)
diversion for mining (Hasdeo Arand) + plantations (oil palm in the NE) + 3.3% lost 2001–2022
forest finance gap $216 billion to 2030 (UNEP)

Environment: forest carbon stock ≈7,285 million t (55% in soil) + shield against storms and floods · Economy: timber, minor forest produce, ≈275 million livelihoods · Society: tribals lose land and forest rights

forest laws <button class="hs chipx" data-h="0">Indian Forest Act 1927</button><button class="hs chipx" data-h="1">FCA 1980 + CAMPA</button><button class="hs chipx" data-h="2">2023 amendment + 2025 rules</button>
geo-tagging + FSI fire alerts + digital forest records
Green India Mission (+5 million ha) + Bonn Challenge (24.1 of 26 million ha done) + native species with survival audits (Miyawaki)
Joint Forest Management (Sukhomajri model) + forest rights
REDD+ payments for standing forests + Japan's Forest Environment Tax

hs.b:
• Colonial law for timber revenue: Reserved, Protected, Village, Private forests + punishes unauthorised use
  • Worked: 2017 amendment (bamboo outside forests freed from transit permits) · Failed: 2019 draft (arms for forest officers) withdrawn after tribal protests
  • Fix: align with FRA (Gram Sabha say) + digitise records

• Centre must approve diverting forest land + compensatory afforestation (CA) for every diversion
  • Godavarman (1996): "forest" = dictionary meaning → FCA covers all forests, recorded or not
  • Failed: Kancha Gachibowli, Hyderabad (2025): urban project vs green lung near KBR National Park → SC put ecology over convenience
  • CAF Act 2016 (CAMPA funds): 85% of CA target met (2019–24) · problems: poor sapling survival, late plans, misuse → geo-tag CA sites (e-Green Watch, PARIVESH 2.0)

• Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam: only forest recorded on/after 25 Oct 1980 protected → ≈28% of actual forest (unrecorded) loses cover + exempts land within 100 km of borders for strategic projects + zoos, safaris = "forestry"
  • SC interim order (Feb 2024): keep the dictionary meaning till deemed-forest records are ready
  • 2025 rules: work can start after Stage-I + critical-mineral mines exempt from public hearing + CA land need not be notified Protected Forest
  • Border exemption: a 100 km line swallows almost all of the NE, high Himalaya and A&N → hotspots open to projects without EIA
  • Fix: notify CA land as Protected Forest + all approvals on PARIVESH + no net loss of forest (as SC asked)

• Restores individual and community forest rights of tribals and forest dwellers; Gram Sabha manages and conserves; overrides the 1927 Act
  • Worked: Mendha Lekha (first community forest rights, 1,800 ha, zero deforestation) + Niyamgiri 2013 (all 12 Gram Sabhas rejected Vedanta)
  • Gaps: community claims pending in 65% of eligible villages (2025) + Gram Sabhas bypassed (Assam oil palm) + SC eviction order 2019 (stayed)
  • Step: FRA cells in tribal districts to clear pending claims (Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan, 2024)
  • Fix: time-bound claims + legal literacy + Gram Sabha consent before any diversion

• Community-protected forest patches (Khasi, Garo hills; 1,200+ mapped by Kerala, 2025)
  • MoEFCC (2025) considering them as community reserves under WPA + nominated to UNESCO as a traditional conservation landscape (2025) + Tribal Ministry wants them counted in India's carbon-sink goal (NDC)

cm.0: ISFR = India State of Forest Report, published every 2 years by the Forest Survey of India.
cm.1: Hasdeo Arand = a dense forest in Chhattisgarh being cleared for coal mines despite Gram Sabha protests.
cm.2: Reserved forest = strictest (no rights unless granted); Protected forest = some rights allowed; Village forest = given to a village to manage.
cm.3: Compensatory afforestation = whoever cuts a forest for a project must pay to plant an equal (or double) area elsewhere.
cm.4: Godavarman case (1996) = SC said 'forest' means any forest in the dictionary sense, whether or not it's in government records.
cm.5: KBR = Kasu Brahmananda Reddy National Park, Hyderabad.
cm.6: CAF Act = Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act: puts the CA money (CAMPA funds) into national and state funds for planting.
cm.7: e-Green Watch = online portal tracking CA plantations; PARIVESH = online single-window portal for environment and forest clearances.
cm.8: Deemed forest = land that looks and works like forest but isn't recorded as forest in government papers.
cm.9: Stage-I = the Centre's in-principle approval for forest diversion; Stage-II = final approval after conditions (like CA) are met.
cm.10: PARIVESH = online single-window portal (2018) for environment, forest, wildlife and CRZ clearances; 2.0 adds tracking of each proposal.
cm.11: FSI = Forest Survey of India (Dehradun, under MoEFCC): publishes the 2-yearly forest report (ISFR) + sends satellite fire alerts to forest staff.
cm.12: Green India Mission (2014): one of the 8 NAPCC missions; grow forest and tree cover on 5 million ha + improve the quality of another 5 million ha.
cm.13: Bonn Challenge = global pledge to restore degraded land; India pledged 26 million ha by 2030.
cm.14: Miyawaki method = planting dense, native mini-forests that grow about 10x faster (Japanese technique).
cm.15: Joint Forest Management = forest department and village share forest protection and its produce (started from Sukhomajri, Haryana).
cm.16: Community forest rights (CFR) = the whole village's right to use, protect and manage its traditional forest, not just individual plots.
cm.17: Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (2024): Centre's mission to bring basic services (houses, water, roads, health) to ≈63,000 tribal-majority villages; sets up FRA cells to settle forest-rights claims.
cm.18: REDD+ = UN scheme that pays developing countries for keeping forests standing and cutting deforestation emissions.

topics.name: Fragile ecosystems

rows.t: carbon stores + storm shields + biodiversity hubs: wetlands 6% of land but 40% of species · mangroves store 3x the carbon of forests · corals hold 25% of marine species · peat holds 5x forest carbon per sq m
protection stuck (Western Ghats ESA draft reissued 6 times since 2014)
warming → bleaching, sea-level rise, algal blooms + invasive species (water hyacinth)
encroachment (India lost 2 of every 5 wetlands in 30 years) + plastic and sewage
shrimp farms, reclamation (Mumbai's mangroves), quarrying, coastal building
their services are unpriced, so they look like "wasteland"
notify and enforce (Wetland Rules 2017, CRZ, ESA)
map and monitor (INCOIS Coastal Vulnerability Index + digital wetland inventories)
restore (MISHTI, artificial reefs) + keep them as bio-shields in coastal plans
community-led use (Mission Sahbhagita, SAIME)
blue carbon credits to pay for protection

hs.b:
• India: ≈7 lakh wetlands, 16 million ha (4.86% of area) + lost 2 of every 5 in 30 years · J&K: 74% of lakes vanished or shrank since 1967 (CAG)
  • Ramsar Convention (1971, Ramsar, Iran; India joined 1982): 100 sites (oldest Chilika, Keoladeo 1981; most in Tamil Nadu) + Montreux Record of threatened sites (Loktak, Keoladeo) + Wetland Cities (Indore, Udaipur)
  • Wise use = keep a wetland's ecological character while people use it (national plans + laws + management + public education)
  • National Wetland Conservation Programme (1985–86) → merged with lake plan into NPCA (2013) + Wetland Rules 2017 (State Wetland Authorities, inventories, no reclamation) + Wetland Wise Use framework 2024 + Mission Sahbhagita
  • India at Ramsar COP15 (2025): "Sustainable Lifestyles for Wetlands" resolution (linked to LiFE), backed by 172 countries

• Salt-tolerant trees of the tide zone: 0.15% of India's area · 3x forest carbon (blue carbon) + cut flood depth 15–20%
  • Worked: Sundarbans during Amphan 2020 (bio-shield) · Failed: Mumbai lost mangroves to reclamation → Bombay HC (2018) made all mangroves protected forest
  • Threats: shrimp farms + coastal building + oil spills, plastic + sea-level rise → half the world's mangroves at risk
  • India: MISHTI (2023) + SAIME (shrimp farming inside mangroves, Sundarbans pilot) → fix: shrimp farms outside mangroves + blue carbon credits

• Corals live with algae (zooxanthellae) that feed them → heat stress → coral expels the algae → turns white · needs clean water + 23–29°C
  • India: Gulf of Kachchh + Gulf of Mannar and Palk Bay + Lakshadweep + Andaman & Nicobar
  • Failed: Lakshadweep hit by the 4th global bleaching (2024) · Worked: Vaan island artificial reefs slowed erosion
  • India: WPA Schedule I + ban on coral and sand in construction + ICRI member → fix: cut runoff + coral cryobank + Biorock (Gulf of Kutch)

• Biodiversity hotspot (endemics: Nilgiri tahr) + UNESCO site (2012) + water tower of the south (Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri)
  • Gadgil Committee (2011) vs Kasturirangan (2013: 37% as ESA) → Karnataka rejected → ESA draft reissued 6 times, still not final
  • Failed: Wayanad 2024 (quarrying in the Gadgil-flagged zone) · Worked: Silent Valley 1984
  • Fix: finalise the ESA with states on board + no quarrying on steep slopes + Western Ghats Ecology Authority

• Peat = plant matter that hasn't rotted for centuries (no oxygen) → 5x forest carbon per sq m; drained peat burns (Indonesia fires) → UNEP Global Peatlands Initiative (UNFCCC COP22, Marrakech)
  • Marine protected areas: Gulf of Mannar marine park, Gahirmatha (Odisha), Lothian island (WB)

cm.0: ESA = Ecologically Sensitive Area, notified under EPA 1986: mining, quarrying, big building and red-category industry banned inside it.
cm.1: CRZ = Coastal Regulation Zone (first 1991, now the CRZ 2019 notification under EPA): limits building and industry near the high-tide line + No Development Zones on the coast.
cm.2: INCOIS Coastal Vulnerability Index: maps how exposed each stretch of India's coast is to sea-level rise, erosion and storm surges.
cm.3: MISHTI = Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes (Budget 2023): plant mangroves on about 540 sq km in 9 states + 4 UTs, using MGNREGS and CAMPA money.
cm.4: Mission Sahbhagita = 'participation' mission: gets local people to protect and use wetlands wisely.
cm.5: Montreux Record = Ramsar's list of sites whose health is getting worse and need urgent attention.
cm.6: Wetland City Accreditation = Ramsar title for cities that protect their wetlands (Indore, Udaipur).
cm.7: NPCA = National Plan for Conservation of Aquatic Ecosystems: one scheme for lakes and wetlands (merged 2013).
cm.8: Blue carbon = carbon stored by coastal and marine ecosystems: mangroves, seagrass, salt marshes.
cm.9: SAIME = Sustainable Aquaculture In Mangrove Ecosystem: shrimp farming that keeps mangroves standing (Sundarbans pilot).
cm.10: ICRI = International Coral Reef Initiative: a partnership of countries and groups working to protect coral reefs; India is a member.
cm.11: Biorock = steel frames with a weak electric current that grow limestone, giving corals a base to regrow. Cryobank = freezing coral cells to revive species later.
cm.12: Gadgil (2011) wanted most of the Western Ghats protected with local say; Kasturirangan (2013) cut it to 37%, focusing on natural landscape only.
cm.13: Western Ghats Ecology Authority = a body Gadgil proposed to manage the whole range across all 6 states.

topics.name: Mining

rows.t: minerals drive the economy, but ≈77% of the world's mines sit within 50 km of Key Biodiversity Areas · sand is the 2nd most used resource after water; India's gap ≈300 million t a year
sand is a "minor mineral" (MMDR Act 1957) → states regulate loosely + Go/No-Go diluted
illegal mining hard to track (Goa, Bellary iron ore)
sand mafia: low entry barrier, high profits
urbanisation → demand for concrete and minerals
mineral revenue vs ecology
each state its own definition and rules (Aravallis)
Forest and land lost + acid mine drainage, heavy metals in water + groundwater falls + dust → lung disease + subsidence and underground fires (Jharia) + tailings dams burst + tribals displaced
Cases: Goa and Bellary iron ore (illegal mining, SC bans) + Jharia coal fires
: EIA + District Survey Reports + Sustainable Sand Mining Guidelines 2016 + Enforcement Guidelines 2020 (mine only what rivers refill) + Deepak Kumar case (2012: clearance even for small sand mines)
drones (Telangana; Punjab with IIT Ropar) + GPS-tracked trucks + digital sand tracking + satellite checks
mine closure plans + reclaim and afforest mined land
Punjab model: farmers legally mine up to 3 ft on their land + registered crusher sites → starves illegal cartels
M-Sand (crushed rock) + recycle construction waste
DMF/PMKKKY money for affected people + star rating of mines

hs.b:
• MoEF + Coal Ministry (2009–10): coal blocks split into "Go" (mining allowed) and "No-Go" (dense forest: >30% gross or >10% weighted forest cover) → about a third No-Go → later diluted ("inviolate forest")
  • Revived: SC in Saranda (2025) ordered a mining plan with Go/No-Go zones from geo-referenced ecological maps → same model asked for the Aravallis

• Oldest fold mountains (≈692 km, Delhi → Haryana → Rajasthan → Gujarat): wall against the Thar + groundwater + Khetri copper
  • Definition row: SC (Nov 2025) accepted "hill = 100 m above surroundings, range = 2+ hills within 500 m" → low hills lose protection → protests → SC stayed it (Dec 2025) + Centre banned new leases (except critical minerals)
  • Fix: one continuous ridge, one definition + Aravalli Green Wall (5 km buffer, 4 states) + Go/No-Go mining plan
  • Worked: Save Aravalli movement (Rajendra Singh → SC halted Sariska mining, 1990) + Mangar Bani no-construction zone

• Riverbed mining changes river flow + lowers groundwater + kills river life + sand mafia violence
  • Fix: replenishment studies (SC) + M-Sand + drones + national aggregates body

• Coastal mining → beach and dune erosion + seawater into aquifers and farms + Olive Ridley nesting beaches lost (Odisha) + fish breeding grounds hit · Alappad, Kerala (mineral sand, "Save Alappad" 2019) · CRZ bans it
  • Coastal erosion: 33.6% of India's coast eroding (West Bengal 63%, Puducherry 57%, Kerala 45%) + coastline re-measured 7,500 → 11,098 km
  • Causes: sea-level rise + stronger cyclones + mangroves lost + sand mining, dredging + ports and seawalls block sand drift + dams cut river silt
  • Fix: mangroves + sand nourishment + Shoreline Management Plans + CRZ 2019 No Development Zones + World Bank K-SHORE (Karnataka) + ICZMP (Odisha, West Bengal) + CMIS

cm.0: Minor mineral = sand, gravel, stone etc. under the MMDR Act; states, not the Centre, give and police these leases, so control is weaker.
cm.1: Acid mine drainage = rain hits exposed rock in mines, turns acidic and carries heavy metals into rivers and groundwater.
cm.2: Tailings dam = a dam holding toxic sludge left after processing ore; when it breaks it floods villages with waste.
cm.3: District Survey Report = each district maps where sand can be mined and how much the rivers refill each year.
cm.4: Weighted forest cover = forest area adjusted for how dense it is, so thick forest counts more.
cm.5: Inviolate forest = forest that should never be opened to mining; the 2010s replacement for No-Go, applied far more loosely.
cm.6: Saranda = Asia's largest sal forest, in Jharkhand's iron-ore belt; SC made the state declare a sanctuary and plan mining by zones.
cm.7: M-Sand = manufactured sand, made by crushing hard rock; replaces river sand in concrete.
cm.8: DMF = District Mineral Foundation: mining companies pay a share of royalty for welfare of mine-affected people (PMKKKY scheme).
cm.9: Sand drift (longshore drift) = waves move sand along the coast; ports and seawalls block it, so beaches beyond them starve and erode.
cm.10: Shoreline Management Plan = a coast-wide plan deciding where to protect, let nature act, or retreat.
cm.11: No Development Zone (CRZ) = a strip from the high-tide line where new construction is banned. K-SHORE = Karnataka Strengthening Coastal Resilience and Economy: ₹840 crore, 7-year World Bank project for erosion control, mangroves, dunes and keeping plastic out of the sea (part of the World Bank's SHORE programme with Tamil Nadu).
cm.12: ICZMP = Integrated Coastal Zone Management Project (World Bank-backed): plans the coast as one unit (hazard lines, mangroves, livelihoods). CMIS = Coastal Management Information System: data network that tracks shoreline change.

topics.name: Climate change (the problem)

rows.t: Earth ≈1.1°C warmer than 1850 (IPCC AR6) + 2024 the warmest year and first calendar year above 1.5°C (WMO) + CO₂ 424.6 ppm at Mauna Loa (2024, record) + warming rate up from 0.18 to 0.26°C (1990–2015 vs 2015–2025) + doubling CO₂ → 2.5–4°C (IPCC AR6) + every extra 0.5°C → more heat extremes, heavy rain, droughts (IPCC SR1.5) + remaining carbon budget for 1.5°C nearly used up
policies lag pledges (≈8% gap between current policies and NDCs) + fossil subsidies

hard-to-abate sectors lack clean tech: steel ≈12% of India's CO₂, cement ≈6%, aluminium ≈2.8% + MSMEs run on fossil fuels (≈135 Mt CO₂ in 2022) + India's share of world emissions 2.5% (1990) → 8.2% (2023) (Mains 365)
<button class="hs" data-h="0">natural causes</button> explain past ice ages, not the fast warming since 1950 (IPCC AR6: unequivocally human-caused)
consumption-heavy lifestyles (answer: Mission LiFE)

fossil fuels (coal ≈71% of India's power generation) + land-use change + methane from rice, livestock, landfills + NITI net-zero report: fossil fuels still 87% of primary energy + ≈1.3 Gt still emitted in 2070 (farms, cement, heavy industry) + 150+ districts live off coal and thermal power (Mains 365)
≈$250 billion a year needed till 2047 (NITI) + island states got only $1 billion of the $100 billion pledged
weak global cooperation: pledges unmet + trade fights (CBAM) → see Climate negotiations
Health: 2.5 lakh extra deaths a year (2030–50, WHO) + heat, disease spread <button class="hs chipx" data-h="2">IPCC impacts</button>

Environment: glaciers, <button class="hs" data-h="4">oceans</button>, <button class="hs" data-h="5">AMOC</button>, extreme weather, <button class="hs" data-h="7">ozone</button> <button class="hs chipx" data-h="3">Glaciers + Himalaya</button><button class="hs chipx" data-h="6">Extreme weather + ENSO</button>
Economy: farm yields fall + adaptation gap: finance far below need
Governance: relief burden + climate litigation grows (MK Ranjitsinh 2024: right against climate change under Arts 14, 21)

Society: climate pushes people into poverty: floods and droughts trap farmers in debt + tribals hit hardest + a 1-unit rise in the services share of state GDP cuts poverty odds ≈1.9% → fix: district-level plans + non-farm jobs + social protection
Society: coasts drown, people move <button class="hs chipx" data-h="9">Sea-level rise + coasts</button><button class="hs chipx" data-h="10">Migration</button>
NAPCC (9 missions) + State Action Plans on Climate Change + National Adaptation Plan + a carbon market
capture and new removal tech <button class="hs chipx" data-h="12">CCUS</button>
also enhanced rock weathering (basalt on fields) + methane feed additives for cattle (3-NOP, red seaweed: cut 30–80%) + Direct Ocean Capture (seawater holds ≈140x more CO₂ per volume than air)

grow the carbon sink (2.29 billion t added by 2021) + MISHTI mangroves + adapt: climate-resilient crops (NICRA, DBW-187 wheat), sponge cities, heat and flood plans in every district + Early Warnings for All (UN, by 2027) + Mission Mausam
remove carbon through land <button class="hs chipx" data-h="13">LBCR</button>
Mission LiFE + direct-seeded rice + landfill methane to bio-CNG (ISRO hotspots: Pirana, Deonar, Ghazipur) + Kerala's Pachathuruthu mini-forests
clean the source: renewables (see Renewable Energy) + green hydrogen (5 million t a year by 2030) + green steel + refuse-derived fuel in cement
municipal green bonds (Ahmedabad) + blended finance + climate budget tagging (Odisha) + parametric insurance for climate losses
global deals → see Climate negotiations + ISA + CDRI

hs.b:
• Milankovitch cycles: Earth's orbit, tilt and wobble shift sunlight over ≈100,000 years → ice ages
  • Solar variability: few sunspots in the Maunder Minimum (1645–1715) → Little Ice Age
  • Volcanoes: Pinatubo 1991 aerosols → ≈0.5°C cooling for about two years
  • Also: ocean currents + plate tectonics, continental drift

• CO₂ + methane + nitrous oxide + CFCs; methane traps ≈84x the heat of CO₂ over 20 years (lives ≈12 years) and caused ≈30% of warming since the Industrial Revolution (IEA 2025) + India not in the Global Methane Pledge (−30% by 2030)
  • Land-use change: forest cleared for farms absorbs more sunlight (south-east Amazon became a net carbon source, 2021)
  • Aerosols: scatter sunlight and change clouds (Indo-Gangetic winter haze)
  • Fossil CO₂ record 10.2 GtC in 2024; India 3rd largest emitter but low per capita (2.9 t vs world 6.7 t)
  • War: militaries ≈5.5% of global emissions (reporting voluntary under Paris) + Ukraine clean-up ≈34.6 billion dollars + Agent Orange stripped Vietnam's forests → Rome Statute: severe war damage to nature = war crime

• Species: up to 54% of land and sea species threatened at 2–3°C · corals: 70–90% die at 1.5°C
  • Systems: permafrost loses 15% by 2100 at 2°C (36–67 billion t of carbon released) + many ecosystems near the limits of adaptation
  • Society: each 1°C → 4.7% more intimate partner violence (UN 2025) + schools shut by heat
  • Belem Health Action Plan (COP30): first health adaptation plan (300 million dollars; 1 in 12 hospitals at risk of climate shutdown)

• Hindu Kush Himalaya warming 0.2°C per decade + 30–67% of glaciers may vanish by 2100 + melt rate doubled since 2000 (Ganga basin −21%, ICIMOD) + Nepal's Yala glacier declared dead + Gangotri retreating ≈20 m a year
  • Why faster: warming fastest at 4,500–6,000 m + black carbon + less seasonal snow
  • Effects: GLOFs and debris flows (Chamoli 2021, Sikkim 2023) + less albedo → more warming + rivers fed less in summer later
  • India: NMSHE + Himansh station + National GLOF Risk Mitigation Programme · World: 2025 Year of Glaciers' Preservation

• Absorb 90% of excess heat + ≈30% of human CO₂ · 2025: record extra 23 zettajoules of heat
  • 4th global coral bleaching (2024) + warmer Arabian Sea → stronger west-coast cyclones (Tauktae 2021, Biparjoy 2023)
  • Ocean acidification + oxygen loss + marine heatwaves 34% more frequent since 1925
  • Nice Ocean Action Plan (UNOC3, 2025): SDG 14 is the least funded SDG · fix: more marine protected areas + Blue NDC Challenge (France + Brazil)
  • India: Deep Ocean Mission + MISHTI mangroves + INCOIS

• Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation: Atlantic currents driven by temperature and salinity (thermohaline) → warm salty water flows north from the Gulf of Mexico, cools, sinks and returns south → keeps western Europe mild
  • Weakening: Greenland melt added ≈5,000 km³ of fresh water → lighter water sinks slower → possible tipping point
  • Collapse → Europe and Arctic cool (≈7°C) + tropical rain belt shifts south → droughts in the Sahel and South Asia, disrupted Indian monsoon + fewer nutrients for marine life
  • Fix: cut emissions + long-term monitoring (ocean bottom pressure)

• El Niño: trade winds weaken → weak monsoon, drought, lower kharif yields
  • La Niña: trade winds strengthen → good monsoon, floods, Bay of Bengal cyclones
  • El Niño–monsoon link weakening → harder forecasts + record heatwaves 2022, 2024 + Himachal floods 2023
  • Super El Niño: Pacific >2°C above normal for long (one forecast for late 2026)

• CFCs, HCFCs release chlorine → Antarctic ozone hole (Aug–Nov) → recovery by 2066
  • Montreal Protocol 1987: ozone-depleting substances cut >98% (worked) → Kigali Amendment 2016: HFCs (strong GHGs) cut 80–85% by late 2040s
  • India: CFCs, halons out by 2010 + HCFC-141b out of foam-making by 2020 (among the first developing countries)
  • India: HFC phase-down 10% (2032) → 85% (2047) + India Cooling Action Plan 2019 (cooling demand −20–25% by 2037–38)

• 1°C warming → global GDP −12%
  • India: yields −4.5–9% (≈1.5% of GDP a year) + rice −10–15%, wheat −20% by 2050 without adaptation + rainfed farm incomes −17–18% (Economic Survey)
  • Kerala floods 2018: ≈₹31,000 crore to rebuild
  • Fix: climate budget tagging in every state + parametric insurance + resilient infrastructure (CDRI)

• North Indian Ocean rising 3.3 mm a year (1993–2017) · 1 m rise → 5.7 lakh ha submerged, ≈71 lakh displaced in India
  • Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata + Sundarbans (up to 80% of mangroves could go; Amphan 2020's storm surge pushed seawater 25 km inland) + 36 million Indians may face persistent flooding by 2100 + Lakshadweep (Kavaratti, Minicoy may lose 60% of land)
  • Indian Ocean region: Maldives (≈1.5 m high) + Bangladesh (0.74 m rise, 2 million+ displaced → migration into Assam, West Bengal) + Jakarta sinking + Sri Lanka (Colombo coast) + Myanmar (Irrawaddy delta) + Pakistan (Indus delta, seawater in Sindh) + Seychelles, Mauritius (beaches, reefs, tourism) → for India: climate migrants + shared fisheries hit + India as first responder
  • Coastal erosion causes: sea-level rise + storm surges + sand mining + dams trap river silt + ports and breakwaters block sand flow + mangroves cleared (new)
  • Coastal erosion fixes: hard (seawalls, groynes) + soft (beach nourishment, dunes, mangroves) (new) · India: HADR, CDRI, MAHASAGAR

• 216 million could be displaced within their countries by 2050 (World Migration Report 2024)
  • Ghoramara, Sundarbans: half the island lost → people moved to Sagar island · Tuvalu–Australia Falepili Union (2023): climate visas
  • India: no law for climate migrants, resettlement left to states (Kosi-eroded villages in Bihar moved with no rehabilitation)

• CCTS 2023: intensity targets for 9 big polluting sectors → buy credits or pay fines + GEI Target Rules 2025: 4 sectors, then 4 more → 208 units cut 3–7% by 2026–27 (penalty 2x credit price)
  • PAT (2012): energy-saving targets for big industry → over-achievers sell ESCerts
  • Green Credit Programme 2023: credits for planting, water, waste · concern: buys credits instead of restoring
  • Article 6 (rules done at COP29): 6.2 country-to-country + 6.4 UN market replaces CDM · issues: greenwashing (CCPA guidelines 2024), weak verification + carbon colonialism (rich buyers pay for cheap offsets in poor countries instead of cutting at home) → fix: third-party verification + Core Carbon Principles
  • World: carbon pricing tools 5 (2005) → 80, covering ≈29% of global GHG, 107 billion dollars revenue (World Bank 2025)

• Capture CO₂ at the source → use it or store it (oil recovery, coal-bed methane, saline aquifers, basalt)
  • Why: hard-to-abate sectors (steel, cement, fertiliser) + blue hydrogen + net zero needs 11.4 Gt stored by 2070
  • India: NTPC Vindhyachal pilot (20 t a day) + Budget 2026–27 ₹20,000 crore over 5 years + target 750 mtpa (NITI) + 5 CCU testbeds for cement
  • Challenges: $100–150 billion cost + injection can trigger quakes + no law yet → fix: national CCS rules + storage maps + hub-and-cluster model

• Land-Based Carbon Removal = using forests, soils, wetlands and farms to pull CO₂ out of the air and store it
  • Methods: reforestation (0.5–10 Gt CO₂ a year, IPCC) + soil carbon + biochar + BECCS
  • Concern: climate pledges rely on ≈1 billion ha of land for it (Land Gap Report 2025) → competes with food and land rights (Mains 365)

cm.0: AR6 = IPCC's 6th Assessment Report (2021–23): the world's main scientific summary of climate change.
cm.1: SR1.5 = IPCC's 2018 special report comparing a 1.5°C world with a 2°C world.
cm.2: Carbon budget = the total CO₂ the world can still emit and stay under 1.5°C. Once it's spent, warming crosses the line.
cm.3: Hard-to-abate = heavy industries (steel, cement, fertiliser) and long-distance transport whose emissions can't be cut easily or cheaply just by switching to renewable power.
cm.4: MSMEs = Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises: small factories and workshops; most still run on coal, diesel or oil and can't afford clean tech.
cm.5: Maunder Minimum = 70 years (1645–1715) with almost no sunspots, so the sun gave slightly less energy and Europe got the 'Little Ice Age'.
cm.6: LiFE = Lifestyle for Environment: India's campaign for mindful use (switch off lights, save water, waste less). It shifts the focus from production to consumption.
cm.7: Primary energy = all energy used in its raw form (coal, oil, gas, sun, wind) before it becomes electricity or fuel. Fossil fuels still supply 87% of India's.
cm.8: GtC = gigatonnes of carbon. 1 gigatonne = 100 crore tonnes.
cm.9: CBAM = Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism: an EU charge on imports based on the carbon emitted making them, so foreign goods pay the same carbon cost as EU goods.
cm.10: ICIMOD = International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (Kathmandu): an 8-country research body for the Hindu Kush Himalaya.
cm.11: GLOF = glacial lake outburst flood: a lake held back by ice or loose rock bursts and floods valleys downstream.
cm.12: Albedo = how much sunlight a surface reflects. Ice reflects a lot; when it melts, the darker ground or sea absorbs more heat, so warming speeds up.
cm.13: NMSHE = National Mission for Sustaining the Himalayan Ecosystem: the NAPCC mission to study and protect Himalayan glaciers, forests and water. Himansh = India's high-altitude glacier research station in Lahaul-Spiti, Himachal.
cm.14: Ocean acidification = the sea absorbs CO₂ and turns slightly acidic, so corals and shellfish struggle to build their shells.
cm.15: Marine heatwave = days or weeks when a patch of sea stays unusually hot; it bleaches corals and kills fish.
cm.16: UNOC3 = 3rd UN Ocean Conference, Nice, June 2025 (France + Costa Rica): its Nice Ocean Action Plan pushes ocean funding, marine protected areas and the High Seas Treaty.
cm.17: Blue NDC Challenge = France and Brazil asking countries to put ocean goals into their climate pledges (NDCs) before COP30.
cm.18: Deep Ocean Mission (2021) = India's mission to explore the deep sea for minerals and life, including a crewed submersible (Samudrayaan).
cm.19: INCOIS = Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services, Hyderabad: ocean, tsunami and cyclone warnings.
cm.20: Kigali Amendment (2016) = add-on to the Montreal Protocol to cut HFCs, the gases in ACs and fridges that don't harm ozone but heat the planet strongly.
cm.21: HCFC-141b = ozone-depleting gas used to blow foam (fridge and building insulation); India phased it out of foam-making from 1 Jan 2020.
cm.22: India Cooling Action Plan (2019) = plan to meet fast-growing AC and fridge demand with less energy and climate-friendly refrigerants.
cm.23: Adaptation gap = the difference between what countries need to cope with climate impacts and the money and action actually there.
cm.24: Climate litigation = taking governments or companies to court over climate harm (e.g. MK Ranjitsinh case, ICJ opinion).
cm.25: Storm surge = a cyclone's winds pile seawater up and push it onto land, like a sudden high tide.
cm.26: Dams trap river silt = sand and mud that rivers used to carry to the coast now settle behind dams, so beaches and deltas get no new sand and shrink.
cm.27: Groynes = low walls built out from the beach into the sea; they trap sand moving along the coast so the beach doesn't wash away.
cm.28: Beach nourishment = pumping or dumping fresh sand onto an eroding beach to rebuild it; dunes = natural sand hills behind the beach that absorb waves.
cm.29: CDRI = Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (India-led, 2019): helps countries build roads, power and hospitals that survive disasters.
cm.30: MAHASAGAR = India's vision for Indian Ocean cooperation: security and growth for all countries in the region (successor to SAGAR) (new).
cm.31: NAPCC = National Action Plan on Climate Change (2008). Its 9 missions: Solar, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Sustainable Habitat, Water, Himalayan Ecosystem, Green India, Sustainable Agriculture, Strategic Knowledge, and Health (the 9th, added later).
cm.32: National Adaptation Plan = a country's plan for coping with climate impacts (heat, floods, crops), prepared under the UNFCCC.
cm.33: CCTS = Carbon Credit Trading Scheme: India's own carbon market. Firms that beat their emissions target earn credits and sell them to firms that miss it.
cm.34: GEI Target Rules = Greenhouse gas Emission Intensity rules: fix how much GHG a sector may emit per unit of product (e.g. per tonne of cement).
cm.35: ESCerts = Energy Saving Certificates: earned by firms that save more energy than their PAT target and sold on the power exchange.
cm.36: CCPA = Central Consumer Protection Authority. Its 2024 guidelines stop companies making false 'eco-friendly' claims (greenwashing).
cm.37: Core Carbon Principles = quality benchmark for carbon credits (real, additional, permanent, verified) set by the Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market.
cm.38: Blue hydrogen = hydrogen made from natural gas, with the CO₂ captured and stored so it doesn't reach the air.
cm.39: Enhanced rock weathering = basalt dust spread on fields reacts with rainwater and CO₂ and locks the carbon away as bicarbonate for ≈10,000 years.
cm.40: 3-NOP (and red seaweed) = cattle feed additives that block the stomach enzymes making methane, cutting it 30–80%.
cm.41: Direct Ocean Capture = pulling CO₂ out of seawater instead of air; seawater holds far more CO₂, so it's easier to extract.
cm.42: MISHTI = Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes: plants mangroves along the coast as a natural wall against storms, with income for locals.
cm.43: NICRA = National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (ICAR, 2011): research and village demos of farming that copes with heat, drought and floods.
cm.44: DBW-187 = a high-yield wheat variety bred to cope with heat (ICAR wheat institute, Karnal).
cm.45: Sponge cities = cities built to soak up rain (parks, wetlands, permeable pavements) instead of flooding.
cm.46: Early Warnings for All = UN goal that every person on Earth is covered by a disaster early-warning system by 2027.
cm.47: Mission Mausam (2024, ₹2,000 crore) = upgrade of India's weather forecasting: more radars and AI, to be 'weather ready and climate smart'.
cm.48: Biochar = charcoal made by burning crop waste with little oxygen; mixed into soil, it locks carbon away for centuries and makes the soil richer.
cm.49: BECCS = Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage: grow energy crops, burn them for power, then capture the CO₂ and store it underground, so the net effect pulls CO₂ out of the air.
cm.50: Pachathuruthu = Kerala's "green islets" drive: local bodies and communities plant small native mini-forests on spare public land.
cm.51: Refuse-derived fuel (RDF) = dry burnable waste (plastic, paper) shredded into fuel for cement kilns instead of coal.
cm.52: Blended finance = public or donor money takes the first risk so private investors are willing to fund green projects.
cm.53: Climate budget tagging = marking each budget item by how much it helps climate action, so a state can track its green spending (Odisha first).
cm.54: Parametric insurance = payout comes automatically when a measured trigger is crossed (e.g. rain above X mm); no damage survey needed (Nagaland 2024).
cm.55: ISA = International Solar Alliance: India–France-led group of sunny countries to spread solar power; HQ in Gurugram.

topics.name: Climate negotiations

rows.t: UNFCCC (Rio 1992) → CBDR-RC (Common But Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities) · India's thread: climate justice + CBDR + finance is a legal duty of the North (Article 9.1) + low per-capita emissions
1997 Kyoto (COP3): binding cuts for rich countries only <button class="hs chipx" data-h="0">Kyoto + CDM</button>
2009 Copenhagen (COP15): 2°C first recognised + voluntary pledges · India (via BASIC): intensity −20–25% by 2020 + no intrusive audits (ICA)
2011 Durban (COP17): mandate for a post-2020 deal for all → Paris · India won "agreed outcome with legal force" wording
2015 <button class="hs" data-h="1">Paris</button> (COP21): every country pledges (NDCs)
2018 Katowice (COP24): Paris rulebook + transparency framework · India kept flexibility for developing countries
2021 Glasgow (COP26): Panchamrit <button class="hs chipx" data-h="2">Glasgow + Panchamrit</button>
2022 Sharm el-Sheikh (<button class="hs" data-h="3">COP27</button>): loss and damage fund
2023 Dubai (<button class="hs" data-h="4">COP28</button>): first Global Stocktake
2024 Baku (<button class="hs" data-h="5">COP29</button>): the finance COP
2025 Belem (<button class="hs" data-h="6">COP30</button>): implementation and forests
Courts <button class="hs chipx" data-h="7">ICJ opinion</button>
Trade <button class="hs chipx" data-h="8">CBAM</button>
pledges not binding + no fossil-fuel phase-out text
technology locked behind IPR
$100 billion never fully met + new goal counts loans + adaptation finance tripled but with no clear baseline
North–South trust deficit + unilateral trade measures (CBAM)
CBDR-RC to guide timelines and finance + grant-based finance + technology access as a right + NDC 3.0 with economy-wide targets + fund loss and damage and the TFFF

hs.b:
• Binding cuts only for Annex I (historical emitters) + market tools: CDM, Joint Implementation, emissions trading
  • India: exempt as a developing country + backed CBDR + one of the largest CDM beneficiaries (credits brought FDI and tech, kickstarted early RE)
  • Credit prices crashed, but keep the approach: CDM now replaced by Article 6.4 (COP29) + India's own CCTS

• Bottom-up NDCs + well below 2°C, pursue 1.5°C + 5-year "ratchet mechanism" + Global Stocktake + transparency framework
  • Art 6 carbon markets + Art 8 loss and damage (no liability) + CBDR "in light of national circumstances"
  • India's first NDC (2030): intensity −33–35% + 40% non-fossil capacity + 2.5–3 billion t extra sink
  • India + France launched the ISA: 125 members, HQ in India + Towards 1000 (1 trillion in solar investment, 1 billion people, by 2030)
  • India's stance: climate justice, not charity + right to eradicate poverty and grow + NDC conditional on finance ($100 billion a year) and technology transfer

• First call to "phase down unabated coal" + cut inefficient fossil subsidies + Paris rulebook done (Art 6) + countries asked to revisit 2030 NDCs
  • Panchamrit: 500 GW non-fossil + 50% of energy from RE + 1 billion t less CO₂ + intensity −45% (all by 2030) + net zero 2070
  • India's updated NDC (2022): intensity −45% + 50% non-fossil capacity
  • NDC 2035: −47% + 60% + 3.5–4 billion t sink
  • Progress: intensity −36% by 2020 + non-fossil 52.57% (Feb 2026) + 2.29 billion t sink by 2021
  • India's stance: got coal "phase-out" changed to "phase-down" in the final text + launched LiFE + asked rich countries for $1 trillion in climate finance (new)

• Loss and Damage Fund agreed (after Pakistan floods 2022, ≈$30 billion loss) + call to reform development banks
  • India: proposed phase-down of all fossil fuels, not just coal + LiFE in the text + submitted its long-term low-emission strategy (LT-LEDS): roadmap to net zero 2070 (green hydrogen, nuclear, E20), conditional on finance
  • Gap: fund set up with no money

• First Global Stocktake: world off track for 1.5°C → "transition away from fossil fuels" (not phase-out)
  • Triple renewables + double efficiency by 2030 (India, China didn't sign: hidden curbs on coal)
  • Loss and Damage Fund running on Day 1 (≈$700 million pledged)
  • Transition text is "just, orderly and equitable": first mention of fossil fuels in ≈30 years of COPs
  • India and China also stayed out of the Global Cooling Pledge
  • India: Global Green Credit initiative + offered to host COP33 (2028) + Global Biofuel Alliance
  • Gaps: loopholes ("transitional fuels" = gas, CCS) + loss-and-damage pledges tiny vs hundreds of billions needed a year → next: stronger NDC 3.0 (2025 round)

• New finance goal (NCQG): $300 billion a year by 2035, counting loans and private money (need: $1.3 trillion)
  • Article 6.4 UN carbon market adopted, replaces CDM
  • Replaces the unmet 100-billion goal (set 2009) + Baku Adaptation Roadmap + first Biennial Transparency Reports + gender programme extended 10 years
  • First Article 6.2 transfer: Switzerland–Thailand (Bangkok e-buses)
  • India: objected at the closing plenary (Chandni Raina) and called it an "optical illusion" + 2035 is too late for the 2030 NDCs + finance must be concessional grants, not loans + wants $600 billion of the $1.3 trillion as grants
  • Next: Baku-to-Belém Roadmap to 1.3 trillion a year

• Tropical Forests Forever Facility ($125 billion goal, ≈$5.5 billion pledged, 20% to Indigenous communities)
  • Adaptation finance tripled to $120 billion by 2035 + Just Transition mechanism + 59 Global Goal on Adaptation indicators + Baku-to-Belem Roadmap to $1.3 trillion
  • Belém Package (all 195 Parties): Belém Mission to 1.5°C + Belém 4x Pledge on sustainable fuels by 2035 (India among launchers) + Belém Health Action Plan (first health adaptation plan) + PACT for coal transitions
  • Also: Global Cooling Pledge reaches 72 nations + halve food waste by 2030
  • India: CBAM = disguised protectionism + TFFF observer + Art 9.1 finance is a legal duty + "COP of adaptation" + welcomed the Just Transition mechanism + rich countries to reach net zero earlier + technology access a right, not a bargaining chip
  • Gap: no fossil-fuel roadmap in the final text

• 23 July 2025 (Vanuatu-led): states have legal duties to cut emissions; failure can be an internationally wrongful act → reparations
  • ITLOS 2024: GHG emissions = marine pollution under UNCLOS
  • India argued CBDR + no new duties beyond UNFCCC and Paris · limit: advisory, not binding

• EU carbon tax on imports from 1 Jan 2026: steel, cement, aluminium, fertiliser, hydrogen, electricity
  • India: cost ≈0.05% of GDP (CSE) + hits MSMEs + heavy paperwork → "disguised protectionism", against CBDR

cm.0: UNFCCC = UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (Rio 1992): the parent climate treaty. COPs are its yearly meetings.
cm.1: CBDR-RC = everyone must act, but rich countries that caused most of the problem must do more and pay more, according to their capacity.
cm.2: Article 9.1 (Paris) = says developed countries 'shall provide' finance to developing ones; India reads it as a legal duty, not charity.
cm.3: Annex I = the list of rich, industrialised countries (USA, UK, Russia, EU…) that had binding cuts under Kyoto.
cm.4: CDM = Clean Development Mechanism: rich countries funded clean projects in developing countries and counted the cuts as credits (CERs). India was a big winner.
cm.5: BASIC = Brazil, South Africa, India, China: a negotiating group of big developing countries.
cm.6: ICA = International Consultation and Analysis: developing countries' self-funded climate actions are only reviewed through consultation, not audited by outsiders.
cm.7: NDC = Nationally Determined Contribution: each country's own climate pledge under Paris, renewed every 5 years.
cm.8: Ratchet mechanism = every 5 years each country must submit a stronger pledge than the last. It can only go up, like a ratchet.
cm.9: Global Stocktake = a 5-yearly check under Paris of whether the world is on track; the first was done at COP28.
cm.10: Loss and damage = money for harm that can't be avoided or adapted to (homes washed away, islands lost).
cm.11: LT-LEDS = Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy: India's 2022 roadmap to net zero by 2070 (green hydrogen, nuclear, ethanol).
cm.12: Global Cooling Pledge (COP28): cut cooling-related emissions 68% by 2050 vs 2022 + efficient ACs and fridges. India stayed out because its cooling demand is still growing.
cm.13: Global Green Credit Initiative (India, COP28): credits for planting on degraded land + an online platform to share ideas. Global Biofuel Alliance (India-led, G20 Delhi 2023, with US and Brazil): spread ethanol and other biofuels worldwide.
cm.14: NCQG = New Collective Quantified Goal: the new climate-finance target that replaces the old 100-billion-dollar goal: 300 billion dollars a year by 2035.
cm.15: Article 6.2 = two countries trade carbon credits directly (e.g. Thailand's e-bus cuts counted by Switzerland).
cm.16: TFFF = a fund that invests money and pays tropical countries every year for each hectare of forest they keep standing.
cm.17: Just transition = moving away from coal and oil without leaving workers and coal regions behind (new jobs, training, support).
cm.18: Global Goal on Adaptation = Paris goal to measure how well countries are coping with climate impacts; COP30 agreed 59 indicators (water, health, infrastructure).
cm.19: PACT = a COP30 initiative to support coal-dependent regions in moving away from coal.
cm.20: ITLOS = International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (Hamburg): the UN court for ocean law.

topics.name: Air

rows.t: weak standards: India's PM2.5 limit (40) is 8x WHO's
monitoring thin in small towns and villages
winter inversion + low wind + north-westerly dust trap pollution
open waste burning (Ghazipur landfill fires)
vehicles + construction dust + stubble + coal plants (Delhi PM2.5: transport 23%, biomass burning 20%, dust 15%, industry 9%, CAQM) <button class="hs chipx" data-h="0">Photochem smog</button>
about <mark>⅔ of Delhi's PM2.5 comes from outside Delhi</mark>
Health: 2nd biggest death risk after high BP + ≈15% of Delhi deaths (2023)
Environment: acid rain + urban heat island
Economy: ≈9.5% of GDP lost (Lancet 2025)
Governance: 66 of the world's 100 most polluted cities are Indian (IQAir 2025)
Society: the poor and outdoor workers breathe it most
raise standards to WHO level <button class="hs chipx" data-h="1">WHO AQG 2021</button>
implement better, target PM2.5 not just PM10 <button class="hs chipx" data-h="2">NCAP</button>
monitors from 25 to 1,600 + SAFAR real-time tracking + trials
scale Delhi's GRAP to other airsheds, move to an <mark>airshed approach</mark> <button class="hs chipx" data-h="4">Delhi model</button>
awareness + end open waste and stubble burning
clean the source: EVs (7.6% share in 2024 → 30% by 2030) + CNG + cleaner industrial fuels + phase out old vehicles
emissions trading (Surat 2019, best practice)
NCR states' joint annual plans + regional caps <button class="hs chipx" data-h="5">Gothenburg 1999</button>

hs.b:
• Classical smog: coal SO₂ + smoke + fog → grey haze, cold humid winters
  • Photochemical smog: NOx + VOCs (vehicles, industry) + strong sunlight → ground-level ozone → brown haze, warm sunny cities
  • Effects: lungs and eyes + SO₂ and NO₂ erode buildings (yellowing Taj) + acid rain
  • Fix: cut NOx and VOCs at source + regional caps (Gothenburg)

• First update since 2005, tighter for most pollutants
  • PM2.5 annual 10 → 5 + PM2.5 24-hour 25 → 15 + PM10 annual 20 → 15 + NO₂ annual 40 → 10
  • New: 24-hour NO₂, peak-season ozone, 24-hour CO limits
  • India's NAAQS (2009): PM2.5 annual 40 = 8x the new WHO level → revise NAAQS

• 2019: cut particulate pollution 40% by 2026 (vs 2017) in 131 non-attainment cities through city action plans
  • Who: CPCB monitors, SPCBs and ULBs implement, MoEFCC funds
  • Problems: P chases PM10, not PM2.5 · N city by city, not airshed · H root causes untouched · F money spent on water sprinkling for dust
  • Fix: target PM2.5 + airshed plans + source apportionment in every city + health-based targets

• Silver iodide, potassium iodide or dry ice sprayed from aircraft → nuclei that pull water vapour into rain · hygroscopic (liquid clouds) vs glaciogenic (supercooled clouds)
  • India: IIT Kanpur trial over Delhi to wash out pollution · World: Dubai for rain
  • Uses: clear smog and dust + rain in drought areas + less hail, wildfire control, more winter snow
  • Concerns: floods and landslides + disturbs natural weather + silver iodide may be toxic + costs unclear → fix: research + environmental safeguards + clear rules

• CAQM Act 2021 (replaced EPCA) runs GRAP for the whole NCR
  • GRAP: 4 stages by AQI: Poor (201–300) → Very poor (301–400) → Severe (401–450) → Severe+ (450+)
  • Beijing model: average PM2.5 cut from 144 to 92 (2015–2024)
  • Polluter pays: environmental compensation (SC, Lodhi Property case)

• Under UNECE Convention on Long-Range Transboundary Air Pollution
  • Caps on SO₂, NOx, VOCs and ammonia
  • Lesson: air crosses borders, so caps must be regional, not city-wise

cm.0: NAAQS = National Ambient Air Quality Standards: India's legal limits for each pollutant in outdoor air (set by CPCB, 2009).
cm.1: VOCs = volatile organic compounds: gases from petrol, paints, solvents; with NOx and sunlight they make ozone smog.
cm.2: NAAQS = National Ambient Air Quality Standards (CPCB, 2009): legal safe limits for 12 pollutants in outdoor air.
cm.3: Non-attainment city = a city that failed to meet national air quality standards for 5 years in a row.
cm.4: Source apportionment = a study showing how much pollution comes from each source (vehicles, dust, industry, stubble).
cm.5: SAFAR = System of Air Quality and Weather Forecasting and Research: real-time air-quality forecasts for big cities (IITM Pune).
cm.6: CAQM = Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and adjoining areas: one body for Delhi's airshed, with power to order and fine. EPCA = the SC-appointed body it replaced.
cm.7: GRAP = Graded Response Action Plan: restrictions that tighten automatically as AQI worsens (stage I to IV: construction bans, truck bans, school closures).
cm.8: Emissions trading (Surat) = factories get pollution permits; those that cut more can sell their spare permits to others, so cuts happen where they're cheapest.

topics.name: Water

rows.t: <mark>water bankruptcy</mark> = long-term use > what nature refills (UNU-INWEH) + India has 18% of people, 4% of fresh water
weak checks on industry and cities + Draft National Water Policy 2020 still not adopted
aquifers mapped late (NAQUIM), little real-time data
climate change (groundwater depletion may triple by 2080)
sea-level rise + storm surges push seawater into coastal aquifers <button class="hs chipx" data-h="0">Seawater intrusion</button>
overuse + nitrogen fertiliser overuse (nitrate now the most widespread groundwater pollutant) + idol immersion during festivals
untreated sewage (>60% enters rivers) + industry (sugar, paper, tanneries, dyeing) <button class="hs chipx" data-h="1">Industrial pollution</button>
farms draw 87% of <button class="hs" data-h="2">groundwater</button>
sewage plants costly to build and run, so few get built
water = State subject, inter-state rivers = Union (Art 262) → many agencies, states fight over water <button class="hs chipx" data-h="3">Urban water governance</button>
Health: cholera, typhoid + blue-baby syndrome, fluorosis, cancers
Environment: eutrophication, dead zones + 296 polluted stretches on 271 rivers (CPCB 2025)
Economy: ≈3% of GDP lost (World Bank) + threat to 75% of wheat and 65% of rice (NITI 2019)
Governance: city water crises (Chennai 2019, Bengaluru 2024) + inter-state disputes
Society: women and girls spend 200 million hours collecting water (UNICEF, global) + 20% of households lack tap water
one national water law <button class="hs chipx" data-h="4">NWP 2012</button>
clean rivers basin by basin <button class="hs chipx" data-h="5">Namami Gange</button>
tap water for every home <button class="hs chipx" data-h="6">Jal Jeevan Mission</button><button class="hs chipx" data-h="7">AMRUT 2.0</button>
: GRACE satellite for groundwater + IN-GRES + AI and GIS to site farm ponds + IoT sensors + RTDAS water-level data (National Hydrology Project)

plan by basin, keep minimum <mark>e-flow</mark> (EU Water Framework Directive), revive water bodies (Mission Kakatiya: 46,531 tanks) <button class="hs chipx" data-h="8">Amrit Sarovar</button><button class="hs chipx" data-h="9">River linking</button>
community action: Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari + Atal Bhujal + Neeru-Chettu (Andhra: 1.2 lakh structures repaired)
clean the source: ZLD + CETPs + less nitrogen fertiliser (natural farming) + drip and sprinkler
water pricing + tradable pollution permits for water (like air emissions trading)
National Water Commission (merge CWC + CGWB, Mihir Shah) + basin authorities

hs.b:
• What: saline seawater moves into coastal freshwater aquifers when freshwater pressure falls; risk along the 7,500 km coast (Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Andhra, Kerala) (new, CivilsDaily)
  • Causes: over-pumping near coasts + sea-level rise, cyclones, storm surges + wetland loss and sand mining (Chennai lost 85% of its wetlands, WWF) + less silt to deltas (dams, river linking)
  • Fix: artificial recharge (recharge wells, subsurface dykes) + caps and licensing on coastal borewells + mangroves + salt-tolerant crops (ICAR-CSSRI rice) (new, CivilsDaily)

• Industry dumps heavy metals (lead, mercury, chromium) + dyes, phenols + hot water
  • Cases: Kali river, UP (sugar mills, distilleries, paper mills → black water, no aquatic life) + Noyyal, Tamil Nadu (Tiruppur dyeing units → farmland infertile, groundwater salty)
  • Fix: zero liquid discharge for textile units + CETPs + online effluent monitoring
  • Law: Water Act 1974 (2024 amendment: fines by adjudicating officers go to the Environment Protection Fund) + EPA 1986 + NGT

• Status (CGWB 2025): 10.8% of units over-exploited (17.2% in 2017) + India ≈25% of world groundwater use
  • Why: Easement Act 1882 ties water to land + cities seal recharge zones + land subsidence in 5 megacities
  • Pollution: 28.3% of samples exceed a BIS limit: nitrate → blue-baby syndrome, fluoride → fluorosis (Nalgonda technique), arsenic → cancers (phytoremediation) + uranium (Punjab, Haryana)
  • Steps: Atal Bhujal + NAQUIM + IN-GRES → next: National Water Commission (Mihir Shah) + groundwater rights apart from land
Atal Bhujal
  • 2019, World Bank-backed, 7 water-stressed states: community-led groundwater management, gram panchayats make water security plans (new)

• Indore contaminated tap-water crisis + many agencies, nobody accountable (Gurugram)
  • ≈38% of water lost as non-revenue water (leaks, theft) + borewell and tanker dependence (Chennai 2019, Bengaluru 2024)
  • Best practice: Rajasthan's Mukhyamantri Jal Swavlamban Abhiyan ("four waters") → groundwater up ≈4%
  • Fix: 100% wastewater treatment and reuse + Integrated Urban Water Management + water budgeting + Jan Bhagidari

• National Water Policy 2012 (earlier 1987, 2002): drinking water and sanitation first, then water as an economic good + minimum ecological flow + basin-level planning
  • Water Regulatory Authority in each state + pricing to save water + a national framework law
  • Draft NWP 2020 (Mihir Shah) not adopted: from building dams to managing demand + groundwater as a common resource
  • National Water Mission (NAPCC): water-use efficiency +20% + basin plans

• NMCG implements: 127 STPs working (Mar 2025) + CETPs for industry
  • Earlier plans (GAP 1985, GAP-II, NGRBA) faltered: P only sewage, not the whole basin · N no e-flow · H states didn't run STPs after building them
  • Now: I NGT 2022 found untreated waste in 60% of the Ganga · F only 69% of funds used till 2024–25
  • Quantum leaps: basin-level management with minimum e-flow + autonomous pollution boards + real-time AI tracking (Ganga digital twin)

• Tap water to every rural household + water-quality monitoring + Panchayats run and maintain it
  • Gap: 20% of households still lack tap water

• Water-secure cities: tap connections to all households in 500 AMRUT cities
  • Outcome-based funding + circular economy of water (treated wastewater reuse)

• 75 water bodies per district, built or revived with people's participation
  • 68,000+ completed (Mar 2025), 46,000 of them under MGNREGS

• NPP 1980 (NWDA): 30 links = 14 Himalayan + 16 Peninsular; Ken–Betwa is the first (MP + UP, Bundelkhand)
  • For: surplus to deficit basins → drought and flood relief + irrigation + hydropower + navigation
  • Against: forests drowned (Panna Tiger Reserve, ≈20,000 people affected) + less silt → deltas sink, seawater intrusion + costly, slow, states fight

cm.0: CGWB = Central Ground Water Board; CWC = Central Water Commission (surface water). Mihir Shah wanted them merged into one National Water Commission.
cm.1: Easement Act 1882 = whoever owns land owns the groundwater under it, so there's no limit on pumping.
cm.2: Phytoremediation = using plants to absorb or break down toxins in soil and water. Bioremediation = using microbes for the same.
cm.3: NAQUIM = National Aquifer Mapping and Management Programme: maps underground water layers to plan their use.
cm.4: IN-GRES = India Groundwater Resource Estimation System: CGWB's online tool that rates every block safe, semi-critical, critical or over-exploited.
cm.5: Non-revenue water = water a city supplies but never bills for: lost to leaks, theft and faulty meters.
cm.6: Eutrophication = fertiliser and sewage overfeed algae; the algae bloom, die and rot, using up oxygen, so fish die (dead zones).
cm.7: CETP = Common Effluent Treatment Plant: one shared treatment plant for a cluster of small factories that can't afford their own. NMCG = National Mission for Clean Ganga (2011): the body that runs Namami Gange. NGRBA = National Ganga River Basin Authority (2009, PM-chaired): the first basin-level body, replaced by the National Ganga Council (2016).
cm.8: GAP = Ganga Action Plan (1985), India's first river-cleaning plan. NGRBA = National Ganga River Basin Authority (2009). NMCG = National Mission for Clean Ganga: the body that runs Namami Gange.
cm.9: E-flow (environmental flow) = the minimum water a river must keep flowing to stay alive for fish, people and the delta.
cm.10: GRACE = NASA–German satellites that measure tiny changes in Earth's gravity to track groundwater loss from space.
cm.11: RTDAS = Real Time Data Acquisition System: automatic stations that send live surface- and groundwater-level data, installed under the National Hydrology Project.
cm.12: NPP = National Perspective Plan for river linking (1980); NWDA = National Water Development Agency, which studies the links.
cm.13: Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari = 'water saving through people's participation': villages build recharge structures with local funds and labour.
cm.14: Neeru-Chettu = Andhra's 'water and trees' campaign to desilt tanks and plant trees with community help.
cm.15: Zero liquid discharge (ZLD) = a factory treats and reuses all its wastewater, releasing none.
cm.16: CWC = Central Water Commission: apex technical body for surface water (dams, flood forecasts). CGWB = its groundwater counterpart. Mihir Shah Committee (2016): merge both into one National Water Commission.

rows.t: India makes ≈4 million t of plastic waste a year (CPCB) + 3rd in the world in single-use plastic
weak enforcement of the single-use plastic ban (thin bags back in markets)
compostable or bio-based plastic is only 1.5% of plastic + few cheap alternatives
plastic never breaks down, only fragments into microplastics
throwaway habits: per-capita plastic waste doubled in 5 years
packaging and FMCG (world makes 460+ million t of plastic a year) + informal recycling <button class="hs chipx" data-h="0">Plastic types</button>
plastic stays cheaper: tariffs on plastics cut to 7.2% while alternatives (bamboo) pay ≈14.4%
: global plastics treaty talks stalled (INC adjourned without consensus)
Health: microplastics enter food and blood
Environment: ≈20 million t of plastic leaks into nature every year (WEF)
Society: waste pickers and coastal communities bear it
strict EPR audits + enforce the ban <button class="hs chipx" data-h="1">SUP ban + EPR</button>
cheap alternatives (KVIC's Project REPLAN, compostables) + National Dashboard on SUP
carry-your-own-bag habits (Sikkim)
replace at source: Mandatory Jute Packaging Act 2010 + recycled-content mandates
Plastic Parks (10 approved, grants up to 50%) + fix tariffs so alternatives are cheaper
industry pacts (India Plastics Pact, Un-Plastic Collective) + a global treaty covering the whole life cycle + synergy with the BRS conventions

hs.b:
• PET: a pet dog drinking from a plastic bottle → everywhere, highly recyclable
  • PVC: plumbing pipes → industrial, toxins, low recyclability
  • PP: double P = Tupperware → goes in the microwave, heat resistant
  • PS: sounds like Styrofoam → crumbles, very low recyclability

• PWM Amendment Rules 2021: single-use plastic items banned from Jul 2022 + EPR on plastic packaging (2022): producers, importers, brand owners answer for the whole life cycle
  • PWM Rules 2024: Panchayats assess local plastic waste + PWM Rules 2026: more recycled plastic in packaging
  • Worked: Sikkim (plastic bags banned in 1998) · Failed: 2022 ban (weak enforcement, few cheap alternatives)

cm.0: INC = Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee, set up by the UN Environment Assembly (2022) to write a global plastics treaty; talks failed at Busan (2024) and Geneva (2025).
cm.1: EPR = Extended Producer Responsibility: the company that sells the product must pay for collecting and recycling it after use.
cm.2: PWM Rules = Plastic Waste Management Rules (2016, amended many times since).
cm.3: Project REPLAN = KVIC scheme that mixes plastic waste with cotton fibre to make carry bags.
cm.4: Plastic Park = an industrial zone with shared facilities for plastic recycling and processing units.
cm.5: India Plastics Pact (CII + WWF India, 2021, first in Asia): companies pledge all plastic packaging reusable or recyclable by 2030. Un-Plastic Collective (UNEP + CII + WWF India, 2019): voluntary company pledges to cut plastic waste.
cm.6: BRS = Basel (hazardous-waste trade), Rotterdam (prior consent for hazardous chemicals trade) and Stockholm (persistent organic pollutants) conventions, run together by UNEP.

topics.name: Oil Spills

rows.t: oil pollution = petroleum released into the sea from tankers, ship accidents, offshore rigs, pipelines and routine discharge (new)
weak checks on cargo declarations and hazardous-goods handling
little real-time detection at sea
rough monsoon seas and cyclones sink ships (MSC ELSA 3 off Kochi, May 2025)
tanker and cargo-ship accidents, fires, collisions + routine discharge <button class="hs chipx" data-h="0">Maritime disasters</button>
insurance disputes delay clean-up
tangled ownership across countries, nobody answers
Environment: oil film blocks light and oxygen → plankton and corals die + coats seabirds and turtles + toxins climb the food chain (new)
Economy: fishing and coastal tourism lose
Society: fishing communities lose livelihoods
Why worse for India: 7,500 km coast + most crude arrives by sea + fragile mangroves (Sundarbans), coral reefs (Gulf of Mannar), turtle nesting beaches (Odisha) (new)
enforce SOLAS + polluter pays + honest cargo declaration
: electronic cargo tracking + satellite detection (RISAT)
bioremediation (Oilzapper, Oilivorous-S by TERI) + natural sorbents (milkweed fibre)
booms and skimmers + standard safety SOPs
National Oil Spill Disaster Contingency Plan (Coast Guard) + MARPOL, UNCLOS

hs.b:
• MSC ELSA 3 sank off Kochi + fire on MV Wan Hai 503 off Kerala (2025)
  • Mauritius, MV Wakashio (2020)
  • Problems: tangled ownership (Liberian flag, German owner, Cyprus manager) + insurance disputes delay clean-up
  • Rules: IMO conventions (SOLAS 1974, MARPOL, IMDG Code) + Merchant Shipping Act 1958 + National Oil Spill Disaster Contingency Plan (Coast Guard)

cm.0: MARPOL = treaty on pollution from ships (oil, sewage, garbage). SOLAS = treaty on ship safety. IMDG Code = rules for carrying dangerous goods by sea. SOLAS 1974 = IMO's Safety of Life at Sea convention (how ships are built, fire safety, lifeboats). IMDG Code = how dangerous goods must be packed, labelled and declared on ships.
cm.1: RISAT = ISRO's Radar Imaging Satellites: see through clouds and at night → spot oil slicks.
cm.2: Oilzapper = TERI's mix of oil-eating bacteria sprayed on spills to break oil down naturally.
